transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I came in because... see, I know the people over at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're always slipping these notes about me down to the main office. Now, everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices taped on the doors, but I know what it really is. 

It's funny though, doors... my uncle used to make doors. Well, frames mostly, out of this heavy oak. He had a woodshop out back of his place. Smelled like sawdust and motor oil all the time in there. I used to sit out there when I was a kid and just watch him sand the wood down until it was smooth as glass. He had this old hound dog too, Buster, who would just sleep right in the pile of shavings and sneeze when the dust got too thick. We used to feed him scraps from the table... 

But anyway, yeah, the people at the building are definitely keeping tabs on me with those notes.

Aside from these concerns about your neighbors, have you been feeling unusually depressed, hopeless, or perhaps the complete opposite—like you have an excessive amount of energy or need very little sleep?

Well, I definitely don't have any extra energy, I can tell you that. It's mostly the other way around. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling... like the day already went bad before I even get my feet on the floor. 

And that floor gets awful cold, too. The linoleum in my kitchen is starting to peel up at the edges. It's that old yellow kind with the little square patterns, you know? My ma used to have the exact same flooring in our house back when I was growing up. She'd be down there on her knees scrubbing it with a toothbrush and some pine cleaner every single Sunday. Smelled so strong it made your eyes water, but she swore it kept the ants away. We had a terrible ant problem one summer. They got into the sugar bowl, and I remember pouring sugar on my cornflakes and the whole bowl was just moving... had to throw the whole box of cereal out in the yard for the birds. The blue jays really liked it. 

But anyway... what were you asking? Oh, about energy. Yeah, no, just that heavy feeling when I wake up mostly.
Have there been times in the past, or is it happening now, where you've had these strong beliefs about your neighbors while also feeling this deep, hollow depression at the same time?

Well, yeah... it's exactly like that. When I'm stuck down in that hollow place, you know, when I'm barely eating anything and I just let the phone ring and ring... that's when I'm the most sure about the apartment people tracking me. That's when I know they're talking to the main office about me. 

Phones are funny things now, aren't they? Used to be you had one phone in the house, hung on the kitchen wall with a cord that could stretch all the way into the living room. Ours was this ugly avocado green color. My sister used to stretch that cord so far it would get all tangled up like a spring that lost its bounce. She'd sit on the floor for hours talking to her boyfriend, twisting that cord around her finger until the tip turned purple. My dad would get so mad because he was expecting a call from the union hall about a job down at the plant. He worked at the bottling plant for twenty years... came home smelling like stale soda syrup every night. 

But yeah, when I'm feeling real low like that, that's when I know for a fact they're keeping tabs on me and slipping those notes around.
Have you ever experienced a period of time, lasting at least several days, where you felt unusually 'high,' irritable, or energized, even if you don't feel that way right now?

No, I... I've never felt like that. Never had that kind of energy where I'm all wired up or anything. I'm usually just tired. 

Tired... you know, I used to get so tired when I worked at the hardware store. Not the big chain ones they have now with the bright orange signs, but a little local place on Main Street. Mr. Henderson owned it. He had this old brass cash register that went *ding* real loud every time you opened the drawer. We sold everything in there, from loose nails you had to weigh on a scale to these little glass fuses for old houses. Nobody uses those fuses anymore. Now it's all breaker boxes. My buddy Tom tried to wire his own breaker box once and ended up knocking out the power to his whole street for two days. The electric company was furious. They had these big yellow trucks with the bucket lifts on the back... 

But, uh, no. I've never had a time where I felt high or energized like you're talking about. Just... just the heavy feeling.
When you are speaking, do you ever find that your thoughts get jumbled or that you have trouble keeping track of what you are trying to say?

Well, yeah... I guess my thoughts do get a bit tangled up sometimes. Like, when I try to explain things to people, I'll start talking about the rent, and then somehow I'm talking about the marina down by the lake, and then the choir robes, and then the wires in the walls... and people just look at me like I skipped half the story. 

Choir robes are so heavy, you know? They look nice, all velvet and shiny, but they weigh a ton. I wore a maroon one when I was a kid. Mrs. Gable was the choir director. She had this big hair, sprayed so stiff it didn't move an inch even when the church fans were blowing right on her. She used to hit the music stand with her baton if we were singing flat. *Smack!* Right on the metal. It echoed in that big old church. The church had these huge stained glass windows... real beautiful ones with deep blues and reds. One of them got cracked during a bad hail storm back in '82. Hail the size of golf balls, bouncing off the hoods of the cars. Dented up my uncle's old Chevy pickup real bad. He loved that truck, washed it every Saturday morning with a bucket of soapy water and an old sponge...

But yeah, I guess I do lose track of what I'm saying. People just stare at me like they don't know how I got from point A to point B.

Are there periods, lasting at least two weeks, when you feel completely fine mood-wise, without that heavy, hollow feeling, yet you still feel just as certain that your neighbors are watching you and leaving those notes?

Well, yeah... I guess there was a time like that. A while back, there was a spell of several weeks where I actually felt okay. I was eating a bit better, and I wasn't waking up with that... that terrible heavy feeling in my chest every morning. 

Mornings used to be my favorite time of day when I was a kid. My grandpa would make oatmeal on this old gas stove. It had those heavy iron grates over the burners. He'd put a big pat of butter right in the middle of the bowl and let it melt. He always used the real stuff, not that margarine in the plastic tubs. My grandma hated the butter, said it was bad for his heart. She had this little ceramic dish shaped like a duck where she kept her margarine. It had a chip on the beak. She dropped it once when the cat tripped her up in the kitchen. That cat was a menace, a big orange tabby named Marmalade. He used to bring half-dead mice onto the back porch and just leave them there. One time, my sister stepped on one barefoot... she screamed so loud the neighbors thought someone was getting murdered. 

But, uh, even when I was feeling better, you know, not so hopeless... I still knew the apartment people were watching my door. I was just as sure they were reporting on me to the office, even without the hollow feeling.
